RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the Planning Commission:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. PC-2026-005, approving Conditional Use Permit (CUP)
  26-0003 and Modification (MOD) 26-0020; and,

  2. Find the project is categorically exempt from environmental review.

BACKGROUND

On November 13, 2014, the Planning Commission approved CUP 14-014 (Resolution
No. PC-2014-039) authorizing a major wireless telecommunications facility, designed as
a 65-foot-high faux water tower with an 18-foot-high, 525-square-foot faux barn
equipment enclosure. The approval was set to expire on November 25, 2024.

Subsequently, before the facility could be constructed, an application to relocate the
wireless facility was submitted on June 14, 2016, as CUP 14-014 Major Modification (MM)
No. 1. The Planning Commission approved the major modification (Resolution No. PC-
2016-039) on September 8, 2016, maintaining the original expiration date of November
25, 2024.
 Staff Report to the Planning Commission
CUP 26-0003 and MOD 26-0020

Pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Section 17.95.040.A (Time Limits), wireless
telecommunications facilities expire after a period of 10 years, unless a time extension is
approved. Since a time extension application was not received prior to the expiration of
the major wireless telecommunications facility, the original entitlement expired, and a new
CUP was required for the continued operation of the existing facility.

Since the original approval of the facility, three modifications were approved to authorize
the relocation, removal, or replacement of existing equipment, installation of new or
upgraded equipment, and construction of new equipment cabinets or enclosures:

    CUP 14-014 MM was approved on September 8, 2016
    MOD 18-035 was approved on July 30, 2018
    MOD 20-012 was approved on March 25, 2020

Applications for CUP 26-0003 and MOD 26-0020 were submitted on March 21, 2026, and
May 21, 2026. After resolution of completeness items, the applications were deemed
complete on June 1, 2026, and scheduled for the August 13, 2026, Planning Commission
hearing.

ANALYSIS

The request is for a CUP to allow the continued operation of an existing major wireless
telecommunications facility for an additional period of 10 years, and for a MOD to include
the removal of six remote radio units and the installation of three four-foot panel antennas
and three Remote Radio Units (RRUs) within the existing tower. The facility consists of a
65-foot-high faux water tank containing the antennas with a base of 784 square feet and
two equipment enclosures, each used by a different carrier, and includes a 525-square-
foot 18-foot-high faux barn equipment enclosure and a 352-square-foot faux railroad
depot equipment enclosure within an approximately 2,784-square-foot lease area. The
lease area is enclosed by an eight-foot-high wrought-iron fence. The facility is centrally

Access

The existing facility is situated within the parking lot of Palmdale Oasis Park and DryTown
Water Park. The existing facility will be accessed via an existing onsite paved pathway
from 40th Street East, with only periodic trips to the site required for routine maintenance
after the upgrades are completed. The facility requires parking for only the intermittent
servicing of the facility, which typically occurs outside of peak hours and is accommodated
by the existing parking lot improvements on the site, ensuring there will be no impact on
any other access points or parking requirements in the vicinity.

CUP 26-0003 and MOD 26-0020

Architecture

The existing stealth telecommunications facility features a 65-foot water tower with a
matte dark brown finish and two 18-foot high themed equipment enclosures surrounded
by a green wrought iron fence. One enclosure is designed as a faux barn with wood siding
painted red, a double door painted green, and the other is designed as a faux railroad
depot with front-facing gable, pale yellow horizontal wood siding and both with contrasting
trim and a standing-seam metal roof. Designed to blend with the DryTown Old West
mining theme, the facility minimizes visual impact. Proposed upgrades will be contained
within the tower enclosure, maintaining the exterior design and site plan as previously
approved, with all equipment concealed within the structures, as shown in Figure 3.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The project is categorically exempt from environmental proceedings pursuant to Section
15301 (Class 1 - Existing Facilities) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
Guidelines. This exemption applies to the operation, permitting, leasing, and minor
alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, and mechanical equipment
involving negligible or no expansion of an existing or former use. The project consists of
the continued operation of an existing major wireless telecommunications facility and
minor equipment upgrades, including the removal and replacement of antennas
concealed within the existing faux water tower. The proposed improvements would occur
entirely within the existing facility and equipment enclosure and would not expand the
existing use, increase the facility’s height or footprint, or result in new ground disturbance.
Furthermore, the project site does not contain environmentally sensitive resources, and
none of the exceptions to the use of a categorical exemption identified in CEQA
Guidelines Section 15300.2 apply. Therefore, no further environmental review is required.

  RESOLUTION NO. PC-2026-005

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  PALMDALE APPROVING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT 26-0003 AND
  MODIFICATION 26-0020; A REQUEST TO ALLOW THE CONTINUED
  OPERATION OF A MAJOR WIRELESS TELECOMMUNICATIONS
  FACILITY AND EQUIPMENT UPGRADES TO AN EXISTING FACILITY
  LOCATED AT DRYTOWN WATER PARK, 4000 EAST AVENUE S, AND
  FIND THE PROJECT IS CATEGORICALLY EXEMPT FROM
  ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

  WHEREAS, Armando Montes of Sequoia Deployment Services Inc., on behalf of
Verizon Wireless, has filed an Application requesting the approval of Conditional Use
Permit (CUP) 26-0003 and Modification (MOD) 26-0020, to allow the continued
operation of a major wireless telecommunications facility for a period of 10 years and
equipment upgrades to an existing wireless telecommunications facility, as described
herein (hereinafter referred to as “Application”); and,

  WHEREAS, the Application applies to a major wireless telecommunications
facility located at 4000 East Avenue S, identified on the Los Angeles County Assessor
roll as Assessor Parcel Number 3052-009-905, legally described in Exhibit A hereto and
shown on the map attached hereto as Exhibit B; and,

  WHEREAS, the facility was approved by the Planning Commission through CUP
14-014 (Resolution No. PC-2014-039) on November 13, 2014, and became operational
on November 25, 2014, with an expiration date of November 25, 2024; and,

  WHEREAS, the relocation of the wireless facility was subsequently approved by
the Planning Commission through CUP 14-014 Major Modification (MM) (Resolution No.
PC-2016-039) on September 8, 2016, maintaining the same expiration date of
November 25, 2024; and,

  WHEREAS, on August 13, 2026, the Planning Commission of the City of
Palmdale conducted a duly noticed public hearing on the Application and concluded said
hearing on that date.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
PALMDALE DOES HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE, RESOLVE, AND ORDER AS
FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. The Planning Commission hereby specifically finds that all of the
facts set forth in the foregoing Recitals are true and correct.

  SECTION 2. The Planning Commission hereby finds as follows with respect to
the environmental document:

  A  Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), the proposed
  project qualifies for a Class 1 Categorical Exemption under Section 15301,
  which exempts operation, permitting, or minor alteration of existing, public
  or private structures, facilities, or mechanical equipment involving negligible
  or no expansion of existing or former use. Facilities) of the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines. This exemption applies to
  the operation, permitting, leasing, and minor alteration of existing public or
  private structures, facilities, and mechanical equipment involving negligible
  or no expansion of an existing or former use. The project consists of the
  continued operation of an existing major wireless telecommunications
  facility and minor equipment upgrades, including the removal and
  replacement of antennas concealed within the existing faux water tower.
  The proposed improvements would occur entirely within the existing facility
  and equipment enclosure and would not expand the existing use, increase
  the facility’s height or footprint, or result in new ground disturbance.
  Furthermore, the project site does not contain environmentally sensitive
  resources, and none of the exceptions to the use of a categorical exemption
  identified in CEQA Guidelines Section 15300.2 apply. Therefore, no further
  environmental review is required.

  B  The custodian of records for the environmental document and all other
  materials which constitute the record of proceedings upon which the
  Planning Commission’s decision is based is the Planning Manager of the
  City of Palmdale. These documents are available for public review in the
  Planning Division of the City of Palmdale, located at 38250 Sierra Highway,
  Palmdale, California 93550, telephone 661/267-5200.

  SECTION 3. Based upon substantial evidence presented to this Commission
during the above-referenced August 13, 2026, public hearing, including public
testimony, and written and oral staff report, this Commission specifically finds as follows:

  A  The proposed use is consistent with the goals, policies, and objectives of
  the General Plan. (CUP)

  B  The request is consistent with the goals, policies, and objectives of the
  General Plan. (MOD)

  The existing major wireless telecommunications facility is located within the
  Public Facility-Park (PF-P) General Plan Land Use designation and zone,
  and is consistent with the policies and objectives of the General Plan as
  shown in Exhibit C. More specifically, the project is consistent with General
 Resolution No. PC-2026-005
CUP 26-0003 and MOD 26-0020
Page 3

  Plan Goal PFSI-4.2, as the existing wireless telecommunications facility will
  continue providing necessary telecommunication services to the area
  without the need to build additional structures nearby. In addition, the
  proposed wireless facility equipment upgrades involve the removal of six
  existing Remote Radio Units (RRUs), and the installation of three new
  RRUs, and three new four-foot panel antennas that will be fully screened
  within the faux water tower. These upgrades will enhance broadband
  connectivity and capacity at the existing wireless facility, employing the
  least intrusive methods to expand coverage in this underserved area.

  C  The proposed use is beneficial and desirous to the community and is
  consistent with the purpose, intent, and standards of this Title and other
  applicable ordinances and codes adopted by the City. (CUP)

  D  The proposed structure or addition meets all applicable ordinance
  standards, including, but not limited to, minimum structure design,
  development standards, and setbacks. (MOD)

  The proposed project is beneficial and desirable to the community as it
  supports the continued operation and upgrade of a major wireless
  telecommunications facility, enhancing local connectivity while minimizing
  visual and environmental impacts. By maintaining and improving an
  existing facility rather than constructing a new one, the project avoids
  greater disruption to the surrounding area and aligns with the intent and
  purpose of the Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC). The project meets all
  applicable ordinance standards, including minimum structure design,
  development standards, and setbacks as demonstrated in Exhibit D. No
  increase in height or the lease area is being proposed. The existing
  antennas will remain screened within the matte dark brown faux water
  tower, and all ground-mounted equipment will be contained within the
  existing red faux barn and faux pale yellow railroad depot equipment
  enclosures. These structures are compatible with the Old West theme of
  the DryTown Water Park, which was approved under CUP 03-06, ensuring
  full compliance with current PMC requirements.

  E  The proposed use and the ongoing operation of the use will not have a
  substantial adverse effect on abutting property or the allowed use thereof,
  and will not generate excessive noise, vibration, traffic, or other
  disturbances, nuisances, or hazards. (CUP)

  F  The site for the proposed use has adequate pedestrian and vehicular
  access. (CUP)
 Resolution No. PC-2026-005
CUP 26-0003 and MOD 26-0020

  G  The request complies with the purpose and intent of all applicable terms
  and conditions of the existing entitlement. (MOD)

  The existing facility is centrally located within the parking lot of Palmdale
  Oasis Park and DryTown Water Park. The proposed use and operation will
  not adversely impact the environment or abutting properties. It will maintain
  its existing design with a matte dark brown faux water tower, faux red barn,
  and pale yellow railroad depot enclosures that minimize noise and blend
  with the park's colors. Access is available via an existing paved pathway
  from 40th Street East, requiring only periodic maintenance visits. Parking
  for servicing is already accommodated in the site’s parking lot, with no
  additional impacts on access or parking. The site is secured by an eight-
  foot wrought iron fence with locked gates and access points, as previously
  approved under CUP 14-014 MM. The proposed use is consistent with the
  policies and objectives of the General Plan, as shown in Exhibit C, and is
  permitted under PMC Section 17.75.020 (Allowed uses – Public facilities
  and open space zones), subject to the approval of a CUP.

  H  The request is listed in Subsection (B) of PMC Section 17.26.040 (Minor
  modifications to approved plans) and does not require new land use
  entitlements, including but not limited to a conditional use permit or site
  plan review. (MOD)

  The proposed modifications involve the removal of six Remote Radio Units
  (RRUs), and the installation of three new RRUs, and three new four-foot
  panel antennas that will be fully screened within the existing faux water
  tower, which does not significantly alter the site plan as approved by CUP
  14-014 MM. The modifications are permitted under PMC Section
  17.26.040(B)(1)(i), which allows minor modifications to previously
